goal: One material that works on any 3D object and any scene.
alternatives: Environment-map-only glass (no scene behind it); a full ray tracer; Heckel's screen-space FBO refraction.
evidence: References 2 and 4 visibly bend what is behind the object, which an environment map cannot do. Screen-space refraction is the article's core technique and maps onto TouchDesigner Render TOPs.
choice: Screen-space refraction from a Refraction TOP plus a separate Reflection TOP, as the user asked. With no Refraction TOP the material falls back to blending with the real background; with no Reflection TOP it uses a built-in studio.
consequence: Correct bending needs a render of the scene without the glass from the same camera. Content outside the frame cannot be refracted in (mirror-repeat hides the edge).
status: implemented

goal: Refraction strength that does not depend on camera, distance or aspect ratio.
alternatives: Heckel's raw refractVec.xy offset; a fixed screen-space scale.
evidence: Heckel's shader adds refractVec.xy straight to the screen coordinates without projecting it through the camera (his scenes can be orbited), so the shift's on-screen direction and size don't follow camera distance, lens or orientation; a fixed screen-space scale makes distant objects distort as much as near ones.
choice: Offset = (refract - eye) in camera space x Thickness, projected with the camera's projection matrix and depth; orthographic cameras skip the depth division.
consequence: Thickness is in scene units and behaves consistently when the camera moves. Still an approximation: it ignores where the ray actually exits the object (the back-face pass improves this).
status: implemented; preview test ior1_is_invisible passes

goal: Smooth rainbow dispersion that is affordable.
alternatives: Heckel's R/G/B or 6-band rygcbv loop (6 texture reads per sample); spectral samples.
evidence: The archived final scene reads the texture 12 times per loop iteration for 6 bands.
choice: One read per spectrum sample with its own IOR and smooth R/G/B weights, normalised per channel. Samples parameter trades quality for speed (default 12).
consequence: Dispersion 0 is exactly neutral at any sample count (preview test). Very high dispersion with few samples shows colour steps; raise Samples.
status: implemented

goal: Frosted blur without grain.
alternatives: Per-pixel random jitter (grainy, effectively dithering, which the user ruled out); many more samples; mipmap-assisted taps.
evidence: First preview with 12 plain taps showed ghost copies (stepped edges).
choice: The frost samples share the dispersion loop on a disc placed by the R2 quasirandom sequence (angle and area from two different irrational steps), and each reads a mipmap level as wide as the gap between samples. The builder sets the samplers to Mipmap Linear; the flat-image reflection blur widens its level by the warp too.
consequence: Continuous blur in the preview: 12 and 32 samples agree within 16/255 (31/255 with ghost copies). The disc's average offset stays near its centre, so frost no longer shifts the image (round 1 used one golden-ratio sequence for angle and radius, which lined the samples up on one spiral arm). If a TouchDesigner build does not provide mipmaps for the TOP, frost falls back to the stepped look and the builder reports a material warning.
status: implemented; preview test frost_converges_with_samples passes; native mipmap behaviour pending

goal: Twelve presets that can also be animated between.
alternatives: Presets baked into the shader; a menu only; a blend slider only.
evidence: User chose 'Both': a menu that loads editable values plus an A/B morph.
choice: Preset menu writes values into ordinary parameters (Parameter Execute DAT). Morph blends every preset-driven uniform toward preset B inside the uniform expressions (presets.py u()).
consequence: Sliders stay meaningful (they are preset A). Morph is continuous and animatable; menus, light direction and scene settings are not morphed.
status: implemented; preset maths unit-tested, native callback pending

goal: Optional, truly optional, measured thickness.
alternatives: Always two passes; depth TOPs; a second colour buffer.
evidence: User asked for a simple single pass plus an optional back-face pass.
choice: render_back only renders while Back-face pass is on (its Render toggle and its sampler binding both follow the toggle). It renders back faces with material_back into rgba32float: rgb = inner surface colour, alpha = distance along the view ray (depth for orthographic cameras). The front pass reads it with texelFetch through a hand-written bilinear filter that only blends covered texels.
consequence: One extra render when enabled, plus 4 texel reads per sample. Measured thickness matches the exact sphere chord at 5 and 50 units and with an orthographic camera; no dark fringe at the back silhouette. The pass shows the nearest back face only, and its aspect must match the glass render.
status: implemented; preview tests pass; native render pending

goal: No refraction smear at silhouettes.
alternatives: Ignore; clamp N.V only in fresnel.
evidence: The IOR 1 invisibility test failed only along silhouettes: interpolated normals there can point away from the camera.
choice: faceCamera() lays such normals back into the view plane, once for the surface normal and again after the liquid ripples.
consequence: IOR 1 reproduces the background exactly (max difference 1/255), with or without Wobble.
status: implemented; preview tests ior1_is_invisible and ior1_is_invisible_with_wobble pass

goal: Robustness where TouchDesigner could not be run.
alternatives: Assume the texture V direction; add a switch.
evidence: Screen UV uses gl_FragCoord with uTDGeneral.viewport, which follows TouchDesigner's own texture rows, but this was not observed natively.
choice: A Flip screen V toggle on the Inputs page, off by default. Since the family sync (C6) the shader also measures the screen orientation at every pixel (screenSign), so a build whose screen rows run the other way bends correctly without the toggle; Flip V is left for inputs that arrive upside down, and flips the base UV and the measured vertical direction together.
consequence: If refraction appears upside down in a build, one toggle fixes it without editing code. The round-1 case (screen measured from the top, textures stored bottom-up) gives the same result as before: the UV flips and view-space up still maps to texture up.
status: implemented; preview tests bends_follow_screen_orientation and flip_v_corrects_upside_down_inputs pass; native orientation pending

goal: Glass that sits inside any scene, with objects in front of it still covering it.
alternatives: Render the glass alone and lay it over the scene with an Over TOP (round 1); discard glass pixels behind a Depth TOP of the scene; draw the glass in a Render Pass TOP on top of the scene render.
evidence: Audit round 2 (C1, D5): the glass-only render has no scene depth, and with a Refraction TOP the glass writes alpha 1, so the Over TOP painted it over foreground objects. Derivative's Transparency article prescribes opaque geometry first, then transparent objects in a Render Pass TOP; the Render Pass TOP keeps its input's colour and depth when Clear Depth Buffer and Clear to Camera Color are off.
choice: Documented workflow: a Render Pass TOP after the scene render, Geometry = the glass objects, Override Material = the component's material. The demo keeps its Over TOP because its backdrop is a flat GLSL TOP with nothing in front of the glass.
consequence: Foreground objects occlude the glass in the user's scene. Override Material also keeps every Geometry COMP free of a material reference, so the back-face pass cannot form a parameter-reference loop. One pass shows one look. Whether the material may sample the scene render the pass builds on is unverified natively; the Over TOP stays the documented fallback.
status: documented; native check pending

goal: Tutorial experiments that give the same state in any order, without touching the user's setup.
alternatives: List every non-preset control in every experiment; reset to defaults inside apply(); reset only the preset values.
evidence: Audit round 2 (A1, D1): apply() only loaded preset values, so 'final' after 'backface' and 'morph' rendered with Morph 0.5 and the back-face pass on, unlike its preview. Audit round 3 (X2): the reset also covered Reflection map and Demo render, so a flat-image Reflection TOP was read as a panorama after any experiment and the demo render the README says to turn off came back on; the docs did not say that light direction, panorama rotation, Flat image warp, Samples and the back-face pass are reset, or that experiments change the shared material.
choice: apply() first resets the preset values, Morph and its target, Samples, Energy conserving, Panorama rotation, Flat image warp, Light direction, Back-face pass, Pause, Fixed time, Teaching stage and Demo spin to their study.json defaults, then loads the preset, sets the menu to custom and applies the overrides. Controls marked setup are kept: Refraction TOP, Reflection TOP, Reflection map (it says how to read the Reflection TOP), Faces, Camera, Glass geometry, Flip screen V, Colour parameters and Demo render (cook cost, not a look). Light direction and panorama rotation stay reset because the experiments' predictions depend on them.
consequence: The article's 'fixes time and every unrelated control' is true natively, and the README and tutorial name exactly what is reset and kept. 'final' restores the default look but stays paused with the Preset menu on Custom. Experiments change the shared material, so the docs suggest a second component for the tutorial. Unit tests apply every experiment after every other one, check that a changed setup (flat image, Demo render off) survives every experiment, and pin the reset list to the documented one.
status: implemented; unit-tested on a fake component; native pending

goal: Inputs fields a TouchDesigner user can drag onto, type into and clear.
alternatives: Python expressions pointing at the demo (round 1); constant relative paths with defaults.
evidence: Audit round 2 (A3, D6): the fields were built in expression mode, so typing a path, clearing the field or Reset to Default did not behave as the README described.
choice: The builder sets each field to the component's relativePath to its demo node, in constant mode, as value and default, and checks that it resolves to that node and stays inside the component; otherwise it falls back to the old expression and prints an inputs warning.
consequence: Ordinary editing; Reset to Default restores the demo. If TouchDesigner resolves these paths differently than expected, the builder says so instead of silently breaking the demo.
status: implemented; native check pending

goal: Liquid motion that stays smooth in installations that run for days, and while its speed changes.
alternatives: absTime.seconds in a float32 uniform (round 1); time modulo an hour (one jump per hour); rate x speed x absTime.seconds wrapped in double precision (round 2); integrating rate x speed per frame in an Execute DAT or a Speed CHOP; integrating it inside the uniform expression's own Python function.
evidence: Audit round 2 (A8, B8): float32 time steps are 62.5 ms after a week, and the noise rows collapse so ripple normals turn grainy. Audit round 3 (X1): Wobble speed is morphed, so rate x speed x absTime.seconds jumped by rate x change in speed x uptime: one frame of a 100-frame Prism Chrome to Violet Gel morph moved uPhase.x by 2.16 lattice units after an hour (normal frame drift 0.0025); in the preview that frame changed the final image by up to 226/255 (film stage 255/255), and nudging Wobble speed by 0.01 by up to 79/255.
choice: The noise lattice repeats every 256 units. presets.py advance() keeps each offset per component: running, every frame adds rate x speed x the seconds since the previous frame, in double precision, wrapped to 0..256 (uPhase); paused, the offset is rate x speed x Fixed time and unpausing continues from it; with speed 0 it holds and never reads the clock. Every call within a frame returns the same value, so both materials agree. The demo spin uses the same integral (spin()). Chosen over an Execute DAT or Speed CHOP because it adds no nodes or unverified parameter names, keeps still looks free of per-frame cooks, and is unit-testable; if the module state is lost (the DAT's text changes) the next frame starts again from rate x speed x absTime.seconds, one jump.
consequence: Seamless wrap and full precision at any uptime; morphing or dragging Wobble speed and Demo spin changes speed, not position: after an hour one morph frame changes the preview no more than at 2 s (max 22 vs 19/255) and a speed nudge changes it by 1/255. Paused captures are unchanged (all 27 previews re-rendered pixel-identical). Hand-wired materials need the same per-frame sum when their speed changes (README).
status: implemented; unit-tested and preview-tested; native frame-by-frame behaviour pending

goal: A real mirror when the user wants one, without changing the accepted looks.
alternatives: Keep additive reflections (Heckel's glow); always remove reflected light from the transmitted light; a toggle.
evidence: Audit round 2 (B12): at Mirror 1 the glass showed the full see-through image plus the full reflection, which the tutorial called a mirror. Making it energy conserving by default would change all twelve presets, which the user has not accepted yet.
choice: Energy conserving toggle on the Reflection page, off by default: on, the see-through and body terms are multiplied by 1 - reflectance.
consequence: Presets unchanged. With the toggle on and Mirror 1, the final image equals the reflection stage (preview test). Retuning presets with it on is an open question for the user.
status: implemented; open question for the user

goal: Colours that look the same in pass-through and linear colour-managed projects.
alternatives: Raw values (round 1); GLSL MAT Colors page (not documented for the MAT); convert in the shader when the project's working colour space is linear.
evidence: Audit round 2 (C6): TouchDesigner 2025.30000+ converts its own colour parameters to the working colour space; ours went through data vectors unconverted.
choice: Inputs > Colour parameters: Auto (project.workingColorSpace; pass-through or older builds keep colours as typed), As typed, or sRGB. The shader applies the sRGB curve to the four colour uniforms when asked (uInputs.w).
consequence: Correct transfer curve in sRGB-linear projects; wide-gamut working spaces get no primaries conversion (slightly more saturated). Default projects are unchanged.
status: implemented; preview test of the sRGB mode passes; Auto pending natively

goal: Family sync C1: glass over a scene render with a transparent background.
alternatives: Keep reading .rgb only (6a58487); the Liquid Glass Blobs formula: keep the sampled alpha as `covered` and compose once for covered and uncovered parts; additionally subtract what the destination already holds at the pixel (reads the Refraction TOP unbent and assumes it is the destination).
evidence: The 6a58487 material wrote alpha 1 wherever a Refraction TOP was connected: over a transparent scene, invisible glass turned the empty background opaque black (preview: 255/255 on 94,405 pixels; Blobs measured the same defect). With the Blobs formula, invisible glass over an alpha-0 scene leaves colour and alpha exactly (max 0/255), an empty scene matches the no-Refraction-TOP blend exactly (0/255), and all twelve presets over the opaque demo scene match 6a58487 exactly (0/255). At alpha 0.5 the glass counts the scene twice (up to 72/255 brighter and more opaque).
choice: transmitted() returns the average sampled alpha; seeThrough = translucency x (1 - covered) x average tint; colour = (mix(body, through x tint, translucency) + glass colour x (translucency x (1 - covered) - seeThrough)) x keep + reflection + glow; alpha = 1 - seeThrough x keep. Where the back-face pass covers the view, covered still comes from the Refraction TOP's alpha at the same spot (fix V1, next entry; the sync first counted the inner surface as covered). The destination-subtraction variant was not adopted: it depends on the Refraction TOP being exactly the image the glass is drawn over.
consequence: Transparent scene renders stay transparent behind clear glass, with or without the back-face pass (since fix V1), ready for compositing over a plate; nothing changes over opaque scenes. Partly covered pixels (antialiased edges, half-transparent objects) look slightly brighter and more opaque behind the glass (documented limit).
status: implemented; preview tests transparent_scene_stays_transparent, empty_scene_matches_no_refraction_top and opaque_scene_matches_pre_sync pass; native pending

goal: Family sync fix V1 (independent check): keep C1's transparent scenes transparent with the back-face pass on.
alternatives: Keep covered = 1 on the inner surface and document it as a limit; read the Refraction TOP's alpha at the same spot as the inner surface (the verifier's preferred fix); store coverage in the back-face pass itself (its alpha holds the distance, so this needs another render target or a sign encoding, both unverified natively).
evidence: sampleBehind() returned vec4(back.rgb, 1.0) wherever the back-face pass covered the view. Preview, invisible Clear Crystal over a scene with alpha 0, compared with the scene alone: back-face pass off 0/255; on 255/255 colour and alpha on 93,845 pixels, the defect C1 removed (6a58487: 255/255 on 94,405). With the scene's alpha: 0/255 with the pass on. Over the opaque demo scene with the pass on, all twelve presets (knot) match the 6a58487 shaders at 0/255 before and after the change, and the back-face capture is unchanged (0/255). At scene alpha 0.5 the pass on now gives the same documented double count as off (72/255; before: 127/255).
choice: sampleBehind() reads the Refraction TOP once and returns vec4(back.rgb, scene.a) where the back-face pass covers the view, scene elsewhere.
consequence: Clear glass keeps an empty background empty with the pass on too; nothing changes over opaque scenes. Over an empty scene with the pass on, the inner surface's own reflections show (colour only, alpha unchanged: Violet Gel up to 156/255 against no Refraction TOP, measured and not asserted). Coverage is read where the view first bends, while the inner colour comes from a second bend, so at the edge of a scene object over a transparent background the two can disagree slightly (not measured; README and tutorial Limits).
status: implemented; preview tests transparent_scene_stays_transparent and opaque_scene_matches_pre_sync now include the back-face pass; unit test test_v1_back_face_branch_keeps_the_scene_alpha; native pending

goal: Family sync C2: the material survives Render Pick passes and renders with extra colour buffers.
alternatives: No branch (6a58487); the documented #ifndef TD_PICKING_ACTIVE / #else form around the vertex body; an #ifdef after the body; a loop over the extra buffers (rejected by WebGL2 in Liquid Glass Flow) or constant indices under #if.
evidence: Derivative's Write a GLSL MAT page (read 2026-11-02, modified 2026-08-05): TDWritePickingValues() writes the pick values and must come before any custom ones; fragColor[TD_NUM_COLOR_BUFFERS], and writing past the buffer count can corrupt output or crash the GPU.
choice: Vertex: all outputs are written as before, then #ifdef TD_PICKING_ACTIVE calls TDWritePickingValues() (the points only move through TDDeform, so its defaults are right). Pixel: fragColor[TD_NUM_COLOR_BUFFERS] with an #ifndef fallback of 1; the glass goes to buffer 0 and buffers 1 to 7 get vec4(0) behind #if TD_NUM_COLOR_BUFFERS > k.
consequence: Pick renders and multi-buffer renders get defined values; with the material's premultiplied blending the zeros leave extra buffers unchanged. compile_glsl.py compiles a picking and a three-buffer variant, and a negative test shows the picking branch is compiled. Native picking and MRT renders pending.
status: implemented; compile variants and preview test extra_colour_buffers_get_zeros pass; native pending. The picking part (TDWritePickingValues() under #ifdef after the whole body) is superseded by family close G6: the documented '#ifndef TD_PICKING_ACTIVE ... #else TDWritePickingValues(); #endif' (below).

goal: Family sync C3 (conditional): a continuous rainbow at the default Samples without dithering, using the Liquid Glass Blobs fan-gap mip level.
alternatives: Keep mip 0 for dispersion (6a58487); fan-gap level (each sample reads a level as wide as the screen gap between neighbouring colour samples, max with the frost gap); a quarter of that gap (what Liquid Glass Blobs ships: blobs.frag, transmitted(), fanGap = 0.25 x the gap); Prism's isotropic footprintLod (not tried: round-2 B7 measured it worse).
evidence: Round-2 B7 method against high-sample references (the 6a58487 shader with 64 and 128 spectrum samples), Dispersion 1, Samples 12, 960 x 540, refraction and final stages, torus and knot, mean error on the pixels the change touches and glass pixels over 32/255. Clear Crystal, torus, refraction: mean 0.80 (6a58487) vs 1.94 (fan gap), 0 vs 0 pixels over 32; Prism Chrome, knot, final: 0.74 vs 1.92. All eight cases: fan gap 2.4 to 2.8 times the error. With Thickness 2.5: Clear Crystal torus refraction 2.21 vs 4.83 and 0 vs 290 pixels over 32; Prism Chrome torus refraction 1.70 vs 4.72, 0 vs 377. The 128-sample reference gives the same numbers within 0.01. Cause: the spectrum weights overlap, so 12 samples are already nearly continuous, and an isotropic mip level also blurs across the fan. Quarter gap (family close G5), measured here with the guard test's metric (960 x 540, refraction stage, torus, Dispersion 1, 12 against 64 samples; checks/results/family-close-measurements.json): at the presets' own Thickness the mean and the glass pixel count do not move (Clear Crystal 0.347, Prism Chrome 0.321/255, as with mip 0). At Thickness 2.5 the mean drops from 1.831 to 1.758 (Clear Crystal) and from 1.320 to 1.317 (Prism Chrome), max 26 and 14/255, 0 pixels over 32/255 either way. The whole gap in the same run: 0.638 and 3.966 with 286 pixels over 32 (Clear Crystal, preset Thickness and 2.5), 0.611 and 3.613 with 394 (Prism Chrome). The members measured the quarter gap too. Liquid Glass Flow: 0 changed pixels at 480 x 270 (its decisions.json, C3: the gap stays below one texel). Liquid Glass Prism: 0 pixels on Clear Crystal and Prism Chrome, mean 2.167 to 2.154/255 on its Spectral Prism (its decisions.json, C3). Liquid Glass Lit: the same quarter-gap numbers as here (its transmitted() is this one line for line); its whole-gap numbers differ by at most 0.001 in the mean and 4 pixels over 32/255 (3.967 with 290 pixels there, 3.966 with 286 here; its decisions.json, C3). Liquid Glass Blobs chose it on its own measurement, with a different metric: its means are over the pixels the rainbow changes (64-sample reference vs Dispersion 0), not over all glass pixels as above. With no fan level its 12-sample mean error against 64 samples is 6.44 to 8.63/255, with 1,059 to 1,935 pixels over 32/255, and a quarter beat no level in all 8 of its cases (its decisions.json). The same metric on this study (family close verifier V5; torus, Dispersion 1, 960 x 540, refraction stage and final image, Clear Crystal and Prism Chrome; checks/results/family-close-measurements.json, v5_blobs_metric): 0.62 to 0.68/255 at the presets' Thickness and 1.58 to 2.22/255 at Thickness 2.5, 0 pixels over 32. The round-2 B7 numbers above, over the pixels the fan gap changes, are in the same range (0.74 to 2.21). So the rainbow error there is about ten times this study's, whichever metric is used.
choice: Rejected: dispersion keeps mip 0 (plus the frost level), with neither the whole gap nor the quarter gap. The whole gap is worse in every case. The quarter gap moves nothing at the presets' own Thickness, so it does not serve C3's goal (a continuous rainbow at the default Samples); its 4% lower mean error on Clear Crystal at Thickness 2.5 does not pay for two extra bend computations per pixel and more code for the tutorial. Preview test dispersion_converges_with_samples pins the measured agreement (12 vs 64 samples: mean within 1/255, within 2.5/255 at Thickness 2.5, no pixel over 32/255); the fan-gap variant fails it (mean 3.97 and 394 pixels over 32). The quarter gap passes that test, so unit test test_g5_c3_record_covers_the_quarter_gap pins the lookup level to the frost gap alone.
consequence: No look change. Raising Samples stays the advice for banding on very thick glass. The rainbow density gap to reference 1 is a single-surface optics limit, not a sampling one (see the Liquid Glass Prism member). Of the family, only Liquid Glass Blobs keeps the quarter gap, because only there does the rainbow spread wide enough for it to matter; Flow, Prism and Lit measured it and rejected it as here.
status: rejected with measurements (whole gap and, since the family close, quarter gap); preview test dispersion_converges_with_samples and unit test test_g5_c3_record_covers_the_quarter_gap guard it

goal: Family sync C4: no dithering anywhere in the output, as the brief asks.
alternatives: Leave the Render TOPs' Dither at its default; set it off in the recipe (strict or lenient); a shader lint only.
evidence: Render TOP and Render Pass TOP pages (read 2026-11-02): parameter `dither` (Advanced page) 'Dithers the rendering to help deal with banding'; the default is not stated. Write a GLSL MAT: TDDither() applies it only when called. Liquid Glass Lit sets dither false on its renders.
choice: render and render_back set dither = False as lenient parameters (a failure becomes a 'dither' build warning); the README tells users to turn it off on their scene render and Render Pass TOP; a unit test bans TDDither and per-pixel noise in all four shaders (gl_FragCoord is read only to place the pixel, hashes take rows, words and letters or object-space lattice cells).
consequence: The component's own output is continuous by construction; users' renders need one checkbox each. Whether a 2025.x build defaults Dither on is a native check.
status: implemented; unit tests pass; native default pending

goal: Family sync C5: no infinities in half-float renders, no NaN from zero vectors, compile errors visible wherever the material compiles.
alternatives: Leave colour uncapped; cap colour and alpha; cap colour only. Ad hoc guards; one safe normalisation helper. Info DATs on materials only; on every render too.
evidence: Liquid Glass Lit measured a highlight of 74,399 against the half-float limit of 65,504. Preview: a light colour of 200,000 gave 7,680 non-finite values in an rgba16float render with the 6a58487 shader. TouchDesigner compiles a copy of a GLSL MAT inside each render that draws it (Lit).
choice: colour = min(colour, 1024) just before the output, rgb only (the back-face pass keeps distances above 1024 in alpha); safeNormalize() for the light direction, the half vector, the eye and the camera axis; every other normalize() argument is non-zero by construction (unit-tested list). The builder adds Info DATs to every Render and Render Pass TOP it creates; inspect() reports render_diagnostics: errors and warnings of the component's renders and of every render in the project whose Override Material, or one of whose Geometry COMPs' Material, is the material.
consequence: Bright values stay finite (max 1024) and display the same. Over the demo, every preset is unchanged (0/255).
status: implemented; preview test output_fits_half_float and unit tests pass; native diagnostics pending

goal: Family sync C6: bends go the right way whatever the build's screen orientation.
alternatives: Assume TouchDesigner's orientation and a manual Flip V (6a58487); Prism's screenSign from dFdx/dFdy of the pixel's projected position; compare the pixel's projected position with its raster position (no derivatives). For Flip V: flip the UV only (round 1, and the merge brief); flip the UV and the measured vertical direction together (Prism).
evidence: Derivative signs: on the knot, 2 to 5 pixels per preset (sliver triangles at grazing silhouettes, whose neighbours in a 2 x 2 block are made-up values) got the wrong sign, up to 50/255 against 6a58487, even with a magnitude check. Position comparison: 0/255 on all twelve presets. Flipped-raster emulation in the preview: the 6a58487 shader differs from the mirror image on about 73,000 pixels; the synced shader only on the about 650 antialiased rim pixels that differ in any correct mirror (the multisample pattern is not mirrored). Flip V: with the measured direction, a UV-only Flip V breaks both Flip V cases (about 72,000 pixels), including the round-1 case it was designed for; flipping both restores them (at most 1/255 or the 650-pixel rim floor).
choice: screenSign() compares where the pixel's camera-space point projects (proj) with where gl_FragCoord places the pixel (same -1..1 range), per axis; a mirrored projection matrix counts too; ties and non-numbers give +1. The result scales toUV (every bend and frost offset) and the flat-image reflection offset. Flip V flips the base UV and the measured vertical direction together, which keeps the round-1 outcome (UV flipped, view up still maps to texture up) and also covers inputs that arrive upside down in a normal raster.
consequence: No look change in TouchDesigner's usual orientation at the sizes measured: 0/255 against 6a58487 on all twelve presets, measured on the knot at 960 x 540, an even size with no pixel on a centre line. Not measured then, and found later by the family critic: in a flipped raster the comparison ties on the centre row of an odd-sized render (both positions 0) and gave +1, so that whole row bent the wrong way (1,480 to 1,596 pixels per twelve renders at 481 x 271; checks/results/family-close-measurements.json); with multisampling a few silhouette pixels near a centre line can also take the wrong sign (the Liquid Glass Flow finding). Superseded in part by family close G2 (below): Liquid Glass Lit's tie-break on the centre lines. The brief's wording 'Flip V stays as the UV-only override' was not followed literally; see co-design.json. Native orientation pending.
status: implemented; preview tests bends_follow_screen_orientation and flip_v_corrects_upside_down_inputs pass; native pending

goal: Family sync C7: glass in a fogged scene takes the Camera COMP's fog.
alternatives: No fog (6a58487); TDFog on the colour as is; the Liquid Glass Blobs form for premultiplied output.
evidence: Write a GLSL MAT: vec4 TDFog(vec4 curColor, vec3 worldSpacePos, int cameraIndex) does nothing while fog is off. Blobs: TDFog takes an unpremultiplied colour, so fogging black gives the fog colour it adds.
choice: Front pass only, after Opacity: colour = TDFog(colour) - TDFog(black) x (1 - alpha), so the glass adds only its alpha's share of the fog. The back-face pass and the teaching stages are not fogged.
consequence: With fog off nothing changes (0/255 against 6a58487). With fog on, the bent scene inside the glass, already fogged in its own render, gets the glass's fog on top: an approximation, documented. The affine form of TDFog is assumed; native fog pending.
status: implemented; preview test fog_adds_only_the_glass_share (with a stand-in fog) passes; native pending

goal: Family sync C8: presets carry over between a 0.1-unit and a 10-unit object.
alternatives: Lengths in scene units only (6a58487); an Object size that multiplies Thickness and Frost and divides Tint density and the pattern frequencies, in the uniform expressions or in the shader; an Object size in SOP units; two values (scene and SOP size).
evidence: Thickness, Frost, Tint density, Wobble scale and the film swirl (a constant 2.5 in the shader) are lengths. With one control and the requirement that Object size 1 changes nothing for every scene, the ripples (measured on the SOP) and the bend (in scene units) cannot both follow a Geometry COMP's scale: the identity at 1 forces one of them to ignore it. Preview: the same torus built at 0.1 and 10 units with the camera moved and Object size set to match renders like the 1-unit torus within 1/255 for Prism Chrome, Frosted Ice, Amber Honey and Oil Slick; the 6a58487 material differs by up to 250/255.

goal: Family close G2: the measured screen orientation must be right on the screen's centre lines too, at odd render sizes and with multisampling.
alternatives: (a) The sync's comparison with +1 on ties. (b) Liquid Glass Lit's tie-break: on a centre line, where the projected and the raster position are both 0, the sign of the projected position's screen derivative decides, only where 1/w changes by less than 10% to the next pixel; the projection's own sign stays inside screenSign(). (c) Liquid Glass Prism's V2 form of the same tie-break: screenSign() returns the raster's direction and the projection's sign is applied after (Prism's viewSign), with the projected position from viewProj x world. Lit also measured and rejected a two-pixel dead zone and a centroid-sampled copy (its decisions.json).
evidence: Lit's survey on this study (scratch survey of the three forms, then the ported test screen_orientation_has_no_wrong_pixels): instrumented copies write the measured sign; torus, knot and sphere; normal and flipped raster; 480 x 270 and 481 x 271; twelve presets at twelve poses per row; one sample per pixel and the 4x multisampled canvas. (a) c94e849: 0 wrong in the normal raster; in the flipped raster 4,625 single-sample, every one on the centre row of 481 x 271 (torus 1,480, knot 1,549, sphere 1,596), and 4,700 multisampled, all but 3 on that row. (b) and (c): identical on every row, 1 single-sample pixel (knot, flipped, odd size, an edge-on centre-line pixel) and 12 multisampled pixels (8 on that row, silhouette pixels near a centre line), 0 in the normal raster.
choice: (b), Lit's form. It measures the same as Prism's on every row here, so neither is measurably better; Lit's keeps the projection's sign inside screenSign(), as this study's form did, so one value scales every offset and the flat-image reflection, and the family's copies stay line for line alike (Flow takes this file). The four new derivatives (ndc and 1/w) are taken at the top of main() with the other two, before TDCheckDiscard().
consequence: At even sizes, such as the captures' 960 x 540, no pixel lies on a centre line and nothing changes. At odd sizes the centre row and column bend the right way in a flipped raster. Known limits, as in Lit: a centre-line pixel on a nearly edge-on surface keeps +1, and with multisampling a few silhouette pixels covering one to three samples of four can take the wrong sign. The C6 record's 'bit-identical previews' is corrected above: it was measured on the knot at an even size only.
status: implemented; preview test screen_orientation_has_no_wrong_pixels and unit test test_g2_centre_line_ties_use_the_guarded_derivative; both fail on c94e849; native orientation pending

All lie within 4 pixels of a centre line. Across the core, Flow, Lit and Prism the largest change is 43/255, at most 7 pixels per row. Looked at 8 times enlarged next to the right-sign render, the core's 43/255 pixel reads as one rim pixel a little darker than its neighbours. Lit's survey measured form (e) over 576 renders: the multisampled residual went from 17 to 1 pixel in the normal raster and from 18 to 16 in the flipped raster. A scratch copy of Lit with a centroid output compiles in glslang (58 of 58, GLSL 4.60 and Vulkan SPIR-V), which says nothing about a TouchDesigner build. Before this round the residual was a known limit here (decision 'Family close G2'), only Liquid Glass Lit listed it as an open question, in its own words, and no native check covered the residual.
choice: (c), the critic's fix. (a) and (b) would change shaders on a qualifier that no TouchDesigner build has run, for pixels that may not be visible; (d) gives no way to settle it. The open question has the same words in the core, Flow, Lit and Prism (co-design.json). validation.json family_close.native_run gains centre_line_residual: render the delivered material and a copy with the orientation set to the right value, take the difference (Composite TOP, Difference; Analyze TOP, Maximum in RGB) and look at those pixels at 100% zoom. The preview test now allows at most 10 wrong multisampled pixels per row (20 before; measured at most 8 here), so the range the question states stays guarded.
consequence: No shader, preset, uniform expression or capture changes. The residual stays as measured until the native check answers. If it is visible, Liquid Glass Lit tries (e) first, with its survey and this check; then the core, with Flow, and Prism. If it is not, the question closes with the native record.
status: implemented as an open family question; native check centre_line_residual pending; unit tests CentreLineResidual (2) fail on the files before this round
